pr_title: Add public MethodInvoker and ConstructorInvoker classes
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/85539

Adds fixed-parameter-count and Span-based Invoke APIs for performance, primarily achieved by preventing the `object[]` allocation for when there are <= 4 parameters. Also, additional, faster, emit-based functions are generated for methods that don't have `ref\out` parameters and meet other constraints. These are also used by the existing Invoke methods so performance there has increased as well.

### Todo
- [x] Add doc for the new public methods
- [x] Create PR for Mono to address unboxing a "true nullable" (currently the PR doesn't generate faster emit-based code for Mono). Done - see https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/89108
- [x] Add tests that layer on top of existing ones; currently this PR just adds a handful of new tests for the new APIs.
- [ ] Add the new benchmarks to the performance repo

How about adding extension methods to `MethodInfo` and `ConstructorInfo` instead of dedicated invoker classes?

> How about adding extension methods to MethodInfo and ConstructorInfo instead of dedicated invoker classes?

The extension methods would have to first check for null "this" and then cast the MethodInfo to RuntimeMethodInfo. It is unnecessary overhead. The only reason why we are adding this is to squeeze performance out of reflection invoke.
Guess it's a typo, an extension method for `Create` wouldn't make sense.

We should try replacing our method info invocation with this and test the performance.

cc @halter73 @BrennanConroy @captainsafia

> Why not make the Invoke methods generic so that people can avoid boxing?

Most often when reflection is used, it's to deal with types you don't know, so you can't provide an appropriate type argument.

Interesting, I guess I use reflection differently. IIRC, any time I've used reflection invoke APIs, I always had strongly typed values and having to use an object array was just an ugly necessary evil. At least we could have both options. the `Span<object>` one for when you don't have strongly typed values and the faster strongly typed one for when you do.

EDIT: Never mind. I had no idea I could just use `Delegate.CreateDelegate` in all these cases instead of reflection. 🤦

Oh wow, it seems I can finally retire my [method invokers](https://docs.kgysoft.net/corelibraries/html/T_KGySoft_Reflection_MethodAccessor.htm) in .NET8+.

I can't wait for trying it out.
Note that `ConstructorInvoker.Invoke()` return value should not be nullable; this will be fixed.
@steveharter are you planning to update DI to use the `ConstructorInvoker`?

review_comments: NIT: By assuming this applyes to all new Invoke methods, this might be good to be added to the public doc

It is not valid to use stackallocated `Span<Object>` before it is protected. The sequence has to be (1) make sure that the span is zeroed out, (2) register it for GC reporting, (3) assign live references to it only after it has been registered for GC reporting.
Thanks. Moved that after the call register.
It doesn't look like this can ever be null based on use cases below, both use `!`. Instead I would make this non-null as it is cleaer.
It can't be null, but due to constructor chaining the analyzer doesn't detect it. It doesn't seem right to add a suppression for that in the main\base constructor since that could affect other cases.
Seems all new public APIs missing docs?
Yes I'll add that to the Todos in the PR description. I didn't want to churn on the API in this (large) PR.

This should take `MethodBase` so that it can be used to invoke constructors on already-allocated types.
